subject: RFP: Inference reservation worksheet & GPU/throughput clarifications
messages:
From: Alice Warren <alice.warren@stellardata.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@stellardata.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: RFP worksheet: required GPU mix & throughput targets

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for taking our RFP. The procurement and platform teams reviewed the worksheet you sent during the kick-off and we have a handful of follow-ups so our Sizing and Procurement committee can sign off. Can you confirm the following items and return a completed worksheet by EOD Friday (our internal deadline):

- Recommended GPU families for steady-state (N clients concurrently): can you provide expected avg p99 latency and tokens/sec per GPU for our target prompts (approx 1.2k token generation, context 2k tokens)?
- Burst profile: how do you recommend handling spikes to 4x baseline QPS? Any suggested reserved vs burst split?
- Reservation economics: example monthly committed vs on-demand cost for a 50% utilization scenario across your suggested mix.
- Fallback plan: if the preferred SKU is unavailable, what compatible variants and perf degradation should we budget for (percent slower / cost delta)?

We attached a target worksheet and the RFP scoring rubric. Let us know if you need clarified workload traces or prompt examples.

Regards,
Alice Warren
Senior Procurement Manager
Stellar Data Inc
(attachment: Stellar_RFP_Worksheet_template.xlsx)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Warren <alice.warren@stellardata.ai>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@stellardata.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 16:28:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFP worksheet: required GPU mix & throughput targets

Hi Alice — thanks, and yes we can get this back quickly. I pulled preliminary numbers with Karthik and attached a filled worksheet (Stellar_RFP_Worksheet_filled.xlsx). A few quick notes for context:

- Assumptions: avg generation length 1.2k tokens, context 2k tokens, model baseline = open-gpt-34B quantized FP16-ish variant.
- Steady-state recommendation: mix of A800-80GB (primary) + A100-40GB (fallback) for latency-sensitive paths; Ampere A800 gives best tokens/sec for long-context workloads in our benchmarks.
- Burst handling: reserve for 1.5x baseline; configure Dedicated autoscaling to burst to shared capacity for up to 4x with priority queuing.
- Economics: worked sample cost rows included in worksheet; Karthik added expected per-token cost at 25%/50/75% utilization.

Before I send the finalized worksheet to procurement, can Karthik and Laura confirm the perf deltas and the recommended reserved/burst split? Stephanie — can you confirm what we usually show as "fallback degradation" in RFPs (we typically quote conservative %).

Thanks — Jordan
Product Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
(attachment: Stellar_RFP_Worksheet_filled.xlsx)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFP worksheet: required GPU mix & throughput targets

Jordan — quick pass from infra sizing / throughput perspective. See inline bullets and the short table below; I'll upload a one-pager to the shared Drive after lunch.

Inline answers:
- GPU families & perf: for the workload you described, we measured (median of internal traces):
  * A800-80GB (primary): ~22-28 tokens/sec for generation at 1.2k, p99 latency ~450-550ms per request when batching is moderate (batch size 4-8).
  * A100-40GB (fallback): ~16-20 tokens/sec, p99 ~700-900ms.
  * H100-80GB (high-throughput reserved): ~30-36 tokens/sec, p99 ~380-480ms (best for heavy reserved commitments).

- Burst profile & reserved split: recommend reserved capacity sized to 60% of expected baseline sustained QPS (so you have headroom for short spikes). Configure autoscaler to pull from an on-demand pool for up to additional 2x sustained burst; for 4x spikes, use shared burst + queuing. This gives good cost/latency trade-off while meeting 99% of your traffic without escalation.

- Fallback compatibility: fallback mapping and perf degradation (relative to A800 primary):
  * A800 -> A100: ~25-30% slower, cost delta -12% per hour (cheaper but higher latency).
  * A800 -> H100: actually faster but more expensive (+30% cost / hour).
  * Quantized variants (int8) on same family: ~5-8% slower but 2x effective density (good for cost saving tiers).

- Example monthly cost row (illustrative, USD / month):
  * Scenario: 24/7 baseline (50% util) with peak allowances to 4x for 2 hours/day.
  * Reserved (A800) 12 nodes: $xx,xxx; On-demand burst (A100/H100 mix) variable: $x,xxx. (See attached redwood_capacity_notes.pdf for spreadsheet extract).

I'll refine numbers after we have Stellar's actual QPS targets per region; if they have distinct EU/APAC footprints we'll split reservations by region.

-Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_capacity_notes.pdf)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFP worksheet: required GPU mix & throughput targets

Adding a couple product/ops items from the console/SLAs side:

- SLA envelope: for Dedicated reservations we can commit to 99.9% uptime for the reserved pool. For the burst/shared layer we don't include an uptime SLA, but we provide performance tracing and fallback policies in the Console that customers can configure.
- Rollout / fallback automation: recommend they enable automatic model variant fallback in the route policy (A800 -> int8 quantized variant -> A100). We'll include recommended circuit-breaker thresholds in the mutual action plan.
- Security/compliance callout: for Private deployments (if they ask) the reservation plan is the same but network egress and KMS integration add a 2–3 week onboarding window.

I'll sign off on the worksheet once we update the cost row to show conservative on-demand multipliers (I recommend +35% to the on-demand bucket for procurement scoring).

-Laura
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 18:45:00 +0000
Subject: RE: RFP worksheet: required GPU mix & throughput targets

Alice / Tom — thanks for the call and the worksheet. Attached is our completed worksheet (Stellar_RFP_Worksheet_filled.xlsx) plus a short notes PDF and a one-page mutual action plan that aligns to your procurement rubric. Highlights:

- Recommended reservation: 12 A800-80GB nodes across us-east-1 (primary) with 4 A100-40GB as a reserved fallback across availability zones. This meets your 1.5k concurrent request baseline with 60% reserved headroom.
- Burst strategy: Dedicated autoscaling to 1.5x baseline, on-demand pool for additional burst up to 4x. We modeled a conservative +35% premium on on-demand for procurement scoring.
- Fallbacks & SLAs: listed compatible variants and expected perf deltas (A100 fallback ~25-30% slower), and we will include automatic route fallback rules in the deployment manifest.
- Next steps / MAP: proposed signature for a 90-day pilot (reserved credits + review at 30/60/90 days). DocuSign link included for pilot SOW (https://app.docusign.com/envelope/EF7642Stellar).

If that aligns, please confirm and we'll route a pilot SOW to your legal/procurement contacts. Happy to hop on a follow-up call Monday to walk through the cost table.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Product Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123
